method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs and street-name labels
why_not_one_block_off: Sheet 50's bottom margin prints '27TH ST.' with adjoining sheet no. 56; its north frontage reads 914 916 918 920 922 924 | 1002-1012 | 1014-1024 | 1102-1112 with avenue-side numbers 2612-2628, i.e. the 26th-27th hundred. Sheet 55's top margin prints '27TH ST.' with adjoining sheet no. 49; its south frontage reads 613-623 | 701-711 | 713-723 | 801-811 with avenue-side numbers 2702-2718, i.e. the 27th-28th hundred. The two sheets are diagonal neighbours (55 covers the 6xx-8xx blocks, 50 the 9xx-11xx blocks) but 27th St is one straight corridor. 26xx north of it, 27xx south of it; the next corridor south on 55 is the printed '28TH ST.' Position recorded is the corridor centreline in that sheet's native raster px, obtained by reading the drawn block-face line off the green native-pixel ruler and adding half the corridor width measured on the same sheet (80 ft streets = 241-246 px, 70 ft avenues = 209-214 px, 20 ft alleys = 60 px, all at ~3.0 px/ft).
